question.text: What is the tax treatment of interest earned on a tax-saving bank fixed deposit (covered under Section 80C)?

answer.text: Interest is taxable each year at the investor's applicable slab rate
Interest is completely tax-free under EEE treatment
Interest is taxed only at maturity as capital gains
Interest is taxed at a flat rate of 10% without indexation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, while the principal invested in a tax-saving bank fixed deposit qualifies for Section 80C deduction, the interest earned is taxable each year. The source therefore classifies the tax-saving bank FD as an ETE (Exempt-Taxed-Exempt-style) product because the return on investment is chargeable to tax annually, unlike PPF which is EEE. The Trap: Candidates often conflate the upfront 80C deduction on the principal with the ongoing tax treatment of returns. The 80C tag does not make the interest tax-free, and tax-saving FD interest is not deferred to maturity or taxed as a capital gain. Note: The exact income-head label (for example, "income from other sources") and any specific post-tax return illustration depend on tax-source material and the investor's bracket, so anchor the answer to the source-backed point that the interest is taxable each year rather than to a particular bracket-specific figure.
